```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 110,
                      eval = requireNamespace("cluster", quietly = TRUE))
library(cpueTargeting)
library(ggplot2)
```

This example applies the whole toolbox to a simulated logbook that looks like
real data: ten species, discrete fishing tactics, trips that combine sets,
rounding, under-reporting, a species recorded under two names, missing
positions, fleet turnover and a closure. Because the data are simulated, the
true tactics and the true biomass trends are known, so we can check what each
step recovers.

# The simulated fishery

`simulate_logbook()` combines the spatial multispecies simulator with the
habitat-based tactics of Winker et al. (2014).

* **Habitats.** Depth increases offshore (shelf to slope) and the substrate is
  patchy: reef patches within sediment. Demersal densities are depth
  preference x substrate affinity, which gives four habitats as continuous
  gradients: shallow reef, deep reef, shallow sediment and deep sediment.
  Pelagic species follow sea temperature and distance offshore and migrate
  seasonally through the area.
* **Tactics.** Each trip chooses a tactic (`Reef` bottom handline,
  `Sediment` bottom longline, or `Pelagic` troll) and a place to fish, by
  expected value. Demersal specialist vessels cannot fish pelagic, pelagic
  specialists only fish pelagic, the other vessels choose freely.
* **Changes over time.** Demersal prices are high in 2000-2007, pelagic
  prices boom in 2008-2015, then prices are neutral; from 2016 the sediment
  gear is banned deeper than 300 m and effort is cut. Some vessels enter later
  (and are more efficient), others leave.

```{r simulate}
sim <- simulate_logbook(seed = 1)
knitr::kable(sim$settings$species[, c("species", "group", "habitat", "depth_mu",
                                      "price")], row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r om-env, fig.height = 4}
sim$Plots$env
```

```{r om-density, fig.height = 4.5}
sim$Plots$density
```

```{r om-tactics, fig.height = 3.5}
sim$Plots$tactics
sim$Plots$effort
```

Nominal CPUE (orange) against the true biomass (black):

```{r om-cpue, fig.height = 5}
sim$Plots$cpue
```

This is what an analyst receives (the tactic is not in the logbook):

```{r logbook}
head(sim$logbook, 10)
```

# Steps 1-4: format and explore

```{r format}
x <- cpue_data(sim$logbook, year = "year", species = "species", catch = "kg",
               effort = "hours", id = "trip", vessel = "vessel",
               lon = "lon", lat = "lat", covariates = "month",
               synonyms = c("Blackspot seabream" = "Pagellus bogaraveo"))
x <- subset(x, !is.na(lon), note = "positions reported")
x
```

```{r fleet, fig.height = 5}
fl <- plot_fleet(x)
fl$vessels
fl$vessel_years
```

```{r species}
plot_species_curve(x, threshold = 0.95)
x <- select_species(x, threshold = 0.95)
```

```{r composition}
plot_composition(x)
```

# Step 6: targeting covariates

```{r targeting}
x <- add_targeting(x)
x$targeting$pca
plot_oc(x)
```

```{r biplot, fig.height = 6}
plot_biplot(x)
tactic_table(x)
```

Here we can check the clusters against the true tactic of each trip (the
tactic of its first set):

```{r check-tactics}
truth <- sim$trips[match(x$data$trip, sim$trips$trip), ]
table(cluster = x$data$FT, tactic = truth$tactic)
table(cluster = x$data$FT, habitat = truth$habitat)
```

Clusters describe the **catch composition**, which reflects both the gear
(tactic) and where it was used (habitat). Trips with two sets, gear
overlap and neighbouring habitats blur the link, so clusters rarely match
tactics one to one; what matters for standardisation is whether the
covariates capture the changes in where and how the fleet fishes.

```{r targeting-plots, fig.height = 4.5}
pt <- plot_targeting(x, res = 0.5)
pt$time
pt$pcs_time
pt$map_tactic
```

# Steps 7-9: standardise two species

## Blackspot seabream (deep reef)

Blackspot seabream lives on deep reefs and is caught mainly by the reef
tactic, whose use changes with prices.

```{r fit-sbr}
fit_sbr <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo",
                    models = c("Base", "Base+S", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_sbr)
```

```{r index-sbr, fig.height = 5}
plot_index(fit_sbr, true = logbook_truth(sim, "Pagellus bogaraveo"))
plot_influence(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")
```

## Dolphinfish (seasonal pelagic migrant)

Dolphinfish is caught by the pelagic tactic and is only present in summer, so
month is added as a cyclic smoother.

```{r fit-dol}
fit_dol <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Coryphaena hippurus",
                    models = c("Base", "Covariates", "Cluster", "DPC"),
                    terms = 's(month, bs = "cc", k = 6)',
                    knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
                    vessel = TRUE, engine = "bam")
cpue_diagnostics(fit_dol)
```

```{r index-dol, fig.height = 5}
plot_index(fit_dol, true = logbook_truth(sim, "Coryphaena hippurus"))
plot_effects(fit_dol, "DPC")$numeric
```

```{r vessels-dol, fig.height = 4}
plot_vessel_effects(fit_dol, "DPC")
```

# Things to try

* `logbook_settings()` lists every setting; change prices, the closure, the
  share of two-set trips (`logbook$two_sets`), the reef share, or make all
  vessels flexible to see how each affects the targeting covariates.
* Compare `n_pc` and the number of clusters, and the species set
  (`select_species(..., pool_other = TRUE)`).
* Fit a delta model (`family = "delta_lognormal"`) for species with many
  zeros.

# References

Winker, H., Kerwath, S.E. and Attwood, C.G. (2014) Proof of concept for a
novel procedure to standardize multispecies catch and effort data. Fisheries
Research 155: 149-159.
